items.title: Tok Mat warns UNHCR: Cooperate on refugee screening in Malaysia or face exit
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — Malaysia should review the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees’ (UNHCR) formal presence in the country if the agency continues to resist cooperation on refugee management, said Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. The foreign minister warned that stringent screening must be a prerequisite before any UNHCR refugee cards are issued, arguing that the current lack of coordination has turned Malaysia into a “magnet” for asylum seekers, NST reported. If Malaysia had its own system, UNHCR would not need to be here,” Mimi said.

items.title: Six held, RM2.98m worth of iron ore and equipment seized in Kelantan mining raid
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, July 29 — The General Operations Force (GOF) detained six men and seized 360 tonnes of iron ore, five vehicles and an excavator worth a total of RM2.98 million during Ops Bersepadu Khazanah at a mining site in Mukim Kuala Nal, Kuala Krai, yesterday. GOF Southeast Brigade commander SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the raid was carried out at 1 pm by intelligence personnel from the GOF 8th Battalion in Pengkalan Chepa in collaboration with the Kelantan Land and Mines Office (PTG). He said inspections at the site found an excavator loading iron ore onto four mototrailers.

items.title: Oil prices up more than 3pct after Iran attacks
items.summary: TOKYO: Oil prices jumped more than three per cent in early Asian trade on Wednesday after the US military said it had intercepted multiple missiles launched by Iran. At around 0015 GMT, US benchmark West Texas Intermediate was up 3.67 per cent at US$82.17 a barrel, while North Sea Brent crude had gained 3.39 per cent to US$86.94. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Police arrest two express bus drivers over meth hidden in bus seat
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, July 29 — Police arrested two express bus drivers on suspicions of possessing methamphetamine found hidden in the back of the driver’s seat during an operation at the Gua Musang Rest and Relaxation Area (R&R) on Monday. Gua Musang district police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said both men, 39 and 46, were arrested by the police after an inspection was conducted on a express bus that both of them were believed to be driving contained methamphetamine hidden the back of the driver’s seat. “Polis also seized several other items believed to be related to the investigation worth an estimated total of RM2,500,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: New Bandar Lawas bridge set to spur growth, open up Southern Lawas
items.summary: LAWAS: The New Bandar Lawas Bridge, which is expected to open to the public in October, is poised to usher in a new phase of urban development in the district by providing a direct link between the northern and southern parts of the town. The bridge is also expected to reduce travel time from about 50 minutes to 25 minutes, improving connectivity and accessibility for the people in the area. Beyond improving accessibility, Ismawi said the bridge would support future residential, commercial and industrial development, while creating new opportunities for trade, tourism and investment in the district.

items.title: Pahang Sultan backs community service for suitable Syariah offences
items.summary: KUANTAN, July 29 — Pahang Sultan Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah has expressed the view that community service sentences should be strengthened as an alternative approach in dealing with Syariah criminal offences. Tengku Mahkota of Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah was also in attendance. The Ruler also congratulated Pahang Royal Council, the Pahang State Secretary’s Office, the Pahang Islamic Religious Department and the Pahang Syariah Prosecution Department for being awarded the SPINE 2026 Excellent Recognition Certificate for Integrity and Governance Management Systems.

items.title: Dollar holds steady as Fed decision looms
items.summary: SINGAPORE: The US dollar was perched near a one-month high on Wednesday, buoyed by safe-haven flows after hostilities flared anew in the Middle East, while traders awaited a key Federal Reserve interest rate decision later in the day. Adding to inflation fears, oil prices were back on the rise after the US military said it intercepted multiple ballistic missiles launched by Iran towards US forces in the Middle East. The New Zealand dollar fell 0.09 per cent to US$0.5782.

items.title: Fahmi: Negeri Sembilan election will be decided by voters, not predictions
items.summary: JEMPOL, July 29 — The outcome of an election is decided by voters, not analysts or political predictions, said Pakatan Harapan (PH) Communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said predictions by certain quarters on the outcome of the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election should be viewed as a challenge for candidates to work harder in winning the seats they are contesting. The PKR Information chief said this when commenting on predictions by Ong, the former Bangi MP, on the potential contests in several seats in the state election.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher versus greenback on improved local sentiment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar today, as market sentiment was boosted by Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour's positive remarks yesterday and expectations of a shift in the US Federal Reserve policy. An analyst said market sentiment improved after Abdul Rasheed said that Malaysia's economy remains well on track to grow by 4.0-5.0 per cent, likely towards the upper end of the range, with manageable inflation in 2026, despite the energy supply shock. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Anwar: Bangladesh seeks Petronas LNG supply to ease gas shortage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Bangladesh has requested assistance from Malaysia, including through collaboration with Petronas, to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) to meet urgent needs arising from the country’s current gas supply challenges, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. In a Facebook post, Anwar said the matter was conveyed to him by Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during a telephone conversation yesterday. “We also discussed economic cooperation, including investment developments involving Axiata and potential strategic cooperation with MMC Port to strengthen economic ties and create more opportunities for both countries,” he added.

items.title: Japan's Takaichi to proceed with food sales tax cut to 1pct, Yomiuri reports
items.summary: TOKYO: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi conveyed to ruling party executives her intention to proceed with a plan to cut the sales tax rate on food items to one per cent from eight per cent for two years from April next year, the Yomiuri newspaper reported on Wednesday. Takaichi met with former prime minister and ruling party heavyweight Taro Aso, and Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) Secretary-General Shunichi Suzuki on Tuesday to convey the plan, the paper said. Aso told Takaichi he would not oppose the tax cut if the prime minister decided to do so, Yomiuri said, citing anonymous government and ruling party sources.

items.title: SK hynix net profit up more than 1,200pct in second quarter
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea's SK hynix posted on Wednesday a second-quarter net profit of 94 trillion won (US$64 billion), a year-on-year rise of 1,242 per cent, driven by the AI industry's explosive demand for its memory chips. The firm's quarterly earnings report also said April-June operating profit jumped 557 per cent from last year to 60 trillion won, while revenue reached 79 trillion won. "With major tech companies increasing their AI infrastructure investments, additional supply requests continue to mount," the statement said.

items.title: Top US oil trade group opposes Hormuz tolls after Gulf-backed voluntary fee proposal
items.summary: NEW YORK: The American Petroleum Institute opposes tolls or transit fees for vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz, the top US oil industry trade group's chief executive Mike Sommers told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday. • Iran has maintained a chokehold on the Strait since the US and Israel began bombing the country in February, sending oil prices soaring. • Congress should also consider opening new SPR sites along the US West Coast, an idea President Donald Trump's administration considered before the start of the Iran war, Sommers said.

items.title: Senate advances sweeping Russia sanctions bill
items.summary: WASHINGTON, (United States): The US Senate advanced sweeping sanctions legislation targeting Russia's energy revenues Tuesday, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy visited Washington to press for stronger action against Moscow. The bill would impose sanctions on Russian officials, oligarchs, financial institutions and the so-called shadow fleet used to evade restrictions on Moscow's oil exports. The vote came hours after Zelenskyy met Trump at the White House and attended the Washington funeral of Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, one of Kyiv's most vocal allies in Congress.

items.title: 2 bus drivers arrested on suspected drug possession at Gua Musang R&R
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Police arrested two express bus drivers on suspicions of possessing methamphetamine found hidden in the back of the driver's seat during an operation at the Gua Musang Rest and Relaxation Area (R&R) on Monday. Gua Musang police chief superintendent Sik Choon Foo said the men, aged 39 and 46, were arrested by the police after an inspection was conducted on a express bus that both of them were believed to be driving contained methamphetamine hidden the back of the driver's seat. "Police also seized several other items believed to be related to the investigation worth an estimated total of RM2,500," he said in a statement.

items.title: Malaysia has shown sympathy towards Rohingya, says activist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia has shown sympathy in the Rohingya issue through humanitarian support, advocacy and efforts to raise awareness internationally, said Rohingya rights activist Zafar Ahmad Abdul Ghani. He said Malaysia had raised the Rohingya issue at international forums, including Asean and the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, and Malaysian groups had also provided assistance and shown solidarity with the Rohingya. He said Malaysia had also continued to show sympathy towards the Rohingya community and support efforts to restore democracy in Myanmar.

items.title: [UPDATED] Four immigration officers among 12 detained over hacked MyIMMs system
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A syndicate believed to have hacked the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) to fraudulently process and approve Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) has been dismantled following a joint operation by the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Immigration Department. MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said those detained comprised two company directors, three foreigners, four Immigration officers, two officers from the department's Information Technology Division, and a policeman. "The operation stemmed from intelligence sharing between MACC's Intelligence Division and the Immigration Department's Intelligence Division, conducted since May across the Klang Valley and Penang.

items.title: 'Magnet for refugees': Malaysia rethinks UNHCR's role [WATCH]
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Malaysia should reconsider allowing the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to maintain an office in the country if the agency continues to refuse to cooperate on refugee management. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said cooperation was crucial to ensure stringent screening before UNHCR refugee cards were issued. She said closing UNHCR's office would not resolve the refugee issue as refugees already in Malaysia would remain.

items.title: Break-in suspect dies, post-mortem reveals blocked artery
items.summary: IPOH: A suspected burglar who allegedly broke into a house in Taman Star here early yesterday died from a blocked coronary artery after a struggle with the house caretaker. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 40-year-old man was one of two suspects believed to have broken into the house in Jalan Building Society at 5am. He said a post-mortem later confirmed that the man died from a blocked coronary artery.

items.title: Oman pitches Iran plan to reopen Hormuz with voluntary fees
items.summary: DUBAI: Oman has presented Iran with a plan backed by Gulf states to manage the Strait of Hormuz, including collecting voluntary fees for using it, a Gulf source and a Western diplomat told Reuters on Tuesday. Iran has denied seeking to resume talks with the United States. Iran has said it would hold fire as long as Washington does.

items.title: Young Negri Sembilan voters want more reasons to stay
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: For many young voters in Negri Sembilan, the challenge is no longer simply finding a job, but also enough reasons to build a future in their hometowns. A 31-year-old food vendor who only wanted to be known as Aina said while job opportunities remained important, the state also needed to make smaller towns more attractive by bringing in modern developments and lifestyle amenities. If there were more opportunities here, many would choose to stay," she said.

items.title: Young voters set to be kingmakers
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Young voters are expected to play the role of kingmakers in Negri Sembilan, with their turnout set to be key, said a political analyst. Universiti Teknologi Mara political analyst Dr Ariff Aizuddin Azlan said youth voters could become the catalyst for change, particularly if they turned out in large numbers on polling day. "Young voters can indeed be regarded as kingmakers or the catalyst for change."

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: Youth to the fore in war of manifestos
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: With 225,853 of the 889,490 registered voters in Negri Sembilan aged between 18 and 29, all major coalitions are placing youth development prominently in their manifestos. Barisan Nasional's youth agenda centres on employment and human capital development, pledging to create 50,000 jobs over five years, including 5,000 high-income jobs in the Malaysia Vision Valley area. Bersatu's youth agenda focuses on easing the transition from education to employment through financial aid, digital skills and entrepreneurship.

items.title: Negri Sembilan polls: Voters seek practical fixes [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Negri Sembilan voters have the chance to send a clear message about the issues that matter to them as the state heads to the polls this weekend. Campaigning has highlighted growing expectations among voters for practical solutions to everyday challenges, ranging from jobs and the rising cost of living to affordable housing and access to higher education. Tawfik said voters ultimately wanted a stable state government, which would be crucial for effective implementation of the state's development plans.

items.title: Freedom of Information law: What does it do?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The government has introduced a proposed law that sets out how Malaysians can request access to information held by federal public authorities. This proposed law — Freedom of Information — establishes the procedures for making requests, how public authorities handles and manages requests. Only Malaysian citizens aged 18 and above may request access to information.

items.title: Trump bids farewell to Lindsey Graham, calls him a war hawk
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump eulogised Republican Senator Lindsey Graham on Tuesday as a fixture of national politics and unflinching foreign policy hawk, as the leaders of Israel and Ukraine joined Washington's most powerful at his funeral. Graham, a South Carolina Republican who died suddenly from a heart ailment on July 11 at age 71, regularly called for an interventionist US role on the world stage. They also recalled Graham's charm working on leaders of US allies.

items.title: Private hospital billing framework to be finalised by year end
items.summary: A FRAMEWORK governing how private hospitals present bills to patients will be finalised by year end. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the move was part of broader efforts to improve price transparency and empower healthcare consumers. "Building on the reference price guides published earlier this year, the Joint Ministerial Committee on Private Healthcare Costs and the Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) are finalising a standardised framework for hospital bill presentation this year," he said at the 2026 APHM International Healthcare Conference and Exhibition.

items.title: Real Madrid in negotiations to buy Leipzig's Diomande
items.summary: BERLIN: Real Madrid are in talks with RB Leipzig to buy Ivorian winger Yan Diomande, a source at the German club confirmed to AFP on Tuesday. Diomande, 19, is under contract until 2030 in Leipzig but has become one of European football's hottest properties, particularly after starring for Ivory Coast at the World Cup. In June, a source at Paris Saint-Germain told AFP that the European champions were interested in signing Diomande.

items.title: Schools ready for 6-year-olds to enter Year 1
items.summary: "The (ministry's) secretary-general (Datuk Wan Hashim Wan Rahim) and I will visit several schools to inspect the facilities and review their preparations," said Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek during the ministry's monthly assembly here yesterday. Fadhlina said the ministry was still receiving enquiries and admission registrations from parents. On another matter, Fadhlina said a school reform pilot programme would begin next week.

items.title: Trump bans new Chinese AI robots, power inverters over security fears
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Trump administration on Tuesday unveiled bans that target imports of new Chinese robots and power inverters, seeking to protect the US AI buildout from national security threats and reshore key industries slated for explosive growth. The restrictions, as first reported by Reuters, show the Trump administration is aiming to safeguard the US artificial intelligence supply chain from Chinese threats of disruption, data theft and cyberattacks, while also driving firms to shift manufacturing to the US "These devices could create supply chain vulnerabilities that could disrupt US economic and national security and could create a cybersecurity risk that threatened American critical infrastructure," the FCC said in a statement. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has warned that Chinese AI firms could face US sanctions for stealing US intellectual property.

items.title: Fuel costs threaten ride-hailing, delivery demand
items.summary: Of those surveyed, 28 per cent said they would switch to cheaper alternatives, such as public transport, driving themselves or cooking at home, while 27 per cent would use the services less frequently. Another 17 per cent would use them only during promotions, and 10 per cent said they would stop using them altogether. Only eight per cent said they would continue using the services, citing convenience.

items.title: Life in prison for US teenager who shot dead four people at school
items.summary: Colt Gray, 16, pleaded guilty to carrying out the September 2024 attack at Apalachee High School in the town of Winder. Gray was 14 years old when he shot dead two 14-year-old students and two teachers, while also wounding nine other people. Superior Court Judge Nicholas Primm sentenced Gray to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

items.title: Netanyahu holds first White House talks with Trump since Iran war began
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the White House Tuesday for his first in-person talks with President Donald Trump since the Iran war began, with the Israeli leader saying they discussed ensuring Teheran does not acquire nuclear arms. The closed-door talks – which the White House described as "positive and productive" – lasted for about an hour and a half and came as Netanyahu and Trump sought to patch over public disagreements on the war. Netanyahu said in a video message after the meeting that it was "one of the best conversations I've ever had with the president of the United States" and that it touched on "our common goal: ensuring that Iran does not obtain nuclear weapons."

items.title: Woman dies weeks after Spain wildfire, taking death toll to 14
items.summary: MADRID: A woman injured in a wildfire in southern Spain earlier this month has died, the hospital where she was being treated said on Tuesday, taking the death toll from the blaze to 14. Fresh wildfires have struck Spain in recent days, ravaging tens of thousands of hectares west of Madrid but so far causing no reported casualties. The woman died at Seville's Virgen del Rocio University Hospital where she was being treated since suffering severe injuries in the blaze, a hospital spokeswoman told AFP, without giving further details.

items.title: Zelenskyy hails 'good' Trump talks on Patriot air defences
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed a "good meeting" with US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House on Tuesday, saying they discussed licences to produce Patriot air-defence interceptors and ways to revive negotiations with Russia. Zelenskyy spent just over an hour with Trump, in talks that came with Kyiv and Moscow intensifying long-range strikes and US-led diplomatic efforts to end the war stalled. Relations between Zelenskyy and Trump have warmed since the start of the US president's second term, with Trump suggesting earlier this month that Ukrainian strikes inside Russia could help end the war.

items.title: ICC faces challenging search for new prosecutor
items.summary: THE International Criminal Court (ICC) faces a challenging search for a new prosecutor after Karim Khan was dismissed, against the backdrop of a United States diplomatic campaign to undermine the court and a rise in states withdrawing from the institution. The African state's announcement came just days after 82 of the court's 125 member states voted to dismiss Khan for serious misconduct. After Khan's removal from office, the court said it will continue to carry out its mandate.

items.title: Central bank's independence to be tested after governor's shock exit
items.summary: JUST as a fragile calm was returning to Indonesian markets, the abrupt resignation of the central bank chief has reignited investor anxiety over policy credibility and political influence in managing Southeast Asia's biggest economy. Perry Warjiyo stepped down on Monday as Bank Indonesia (BI) governor after eight years for personal reasons, with Destry Damayanti, a senior deputy governor, appointed as interim governor, bringing some level of continuity, for now. At stake is whether Indonesia's policy path may bend to political pressure even as the rupiah hovers near record lows and investor confidence over Indonesia's fiscal health under President Prabowo Subianto continues to erode.

items.title: Defence minister: Local defence industry must grow to cut import reliance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The development of the local defence industry must continue to be strengthened to reduce the country’s dependence on imports while enhancing domestic manufacturing capabilities, says Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. Mohamed Khaled said efforts to develop local components must be intensified to ensure the entire defence industry supply chain could be established domestically. “The effort is in line with the government’s and the Defence Ministry’s objectives under the National Defence Industry Policy (DIPN) to strengthen the local defence industry, meet the country’s strategic requirements and position Malaysia as part of the global defence industry supply chain,” he added.

items.title: HR minister: Locals should be first priority when hiring, foreign labour only when necessary
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — Malaysians must be given priority for available jobs before employers turn to foreign workers, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said. He said the policy is in line with the Human Resources Ministry’s primary objective of ensuring employment opportunities are offered to local workers first. “As the Human Resources Minister, my foremost priority is jobs for Malaysians.

items.title: Businessman: Bumi contractor’s RM1m to Bersatu was ‘reward’ after getting RM141m govt project, tapped Muhyiddin’s golf buddy’s help
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Bumiputera contractor Nepturis Sdn Bhd had given RM1 million to political party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (PPBM) in 2022 as a “reward” after the company was awarded a RM141 million government project, instead of as a “donation”, a businessman told the High Court today. Lian said he had asked Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad, whom he had heard was close to and frequently played golf with Muhyiddin, to help get Muhyiddin’s written support for Nepturis’ application for the RM141 million project. Lian, 55, said this as the 21st prosecution witness in Bersatu president and former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.

items.title: Selangor MB Amirudin Shari orders crackdown on purported unauthorised settlements in Setia Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 28 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has ordered the local authorities to take immediate action concerning a purported illegal foreign settlement in Setia Alam. He said the directive followed a decision made at the Selangor State Security Working Committee meeting a few days ago, which stipulated that enforcement action must be taken if land encroachment is found. According to Amirudin, the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) will take action, including issuing notices to the landowners concerned and determining whether the land belongs to the government or private owners.

items.title: PPR Seri Pantai gets RM2.59m worth of upgrading works from DBKL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has allocated a total of RM2.59 million to carry out maintenance and upgrading works at the Seri Pantai People’s Housing Programme (PPR). PPR Seri Pantai, which began operating in 1998, has 936 housing units, including 615 rental units and 321 owner-occupied units. The project forms part of the federal government’s RM300 million allocation to refurbish and maintain public housing (PA) and People’s Housing Programme or Program Perumahan Rakyat (PPR) schemes managed by DBKL across Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Former unit trust consultant jailed 18 months, fined RM2m for investment fraud
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — A former unit trust consultant was sentenced to 18 months in prison and fined a total of RM2 million by two Sessions Courts here today after pleading guilty to cheating two men in connection with investments in securities. Judge Azrul Darus sentenced Amran Mohd Amin, 59, to 18 months in prison and a fine of RM1 million, or six months’ imprisonment in default, for the first charge. However, the two prison terms will run concurrently from the date of Amran’s arrest on September 8, 2025.

items.title: After nearly three years, Johor police reclassify baby’s death as murder, father named main suspect
items.summary: The probe also identified the 18-month-old victim’s father as the main suspect. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report on the case was received from a doctor attached to the Sultan Ismail Hospital’s (HSI) emergency department here on September 13, 2023. He said the victim, who was unconscious, was brought to the hospital by his 40-year-old father.

items.title: Bahrain to cover F1 rights fees for Sepang race, says SIC
items.summary: SEPANG, July 28 — Bahrain will fully bear the Formula One (F1) rights fees of US$70 million (RM298 million) to US$80 million for the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, according to SIC. SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif said this arrangement was agreed through cooperation between SIC and the Bahrain International Circuit (BIC). However, Azhan Shafriman said Malaysia still needs to share the cost of local preparations of around RM40 million to ensure the circuit meets Formula One specifications.

items.title: Transport Ministry says Putrajaya monorail project not viable to revive
items.summary: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) in a written response posted on the Parliament website today said the findings were obtained through the Public Transport Study in Putrajaya, Cyberjaya, Bangi and Kajang which also assessed the feasibility of the monorail system. Alternatively, the ministry said that the Nadi Putra Bus service currently involves seven routes with 26 buses and records an average of 2,246 passengers on weekdays. The shuttle bus service includes two routes with eight buses and an average of 1,173 passengers, while the Rapid On-Demand involves three routes with nine vans and an average of 315 passengers on weekdays.

items.title: Malaysia registers 26 rare disease medicines since 2020, says Health Ministry
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — A total of 26 medicines for rare diseases had been registered in Malaysia as of April this year, from none before 2020, the Dewan Negara was told today. Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib said the milestone reflects the Ministry of Health's (MOH) ongoing efforts to improve access to medicines and treatment for patients with rare diseases. Hanifah Hajar said 529 types of rare diseases have been identified and included in the Malaysian Rare Disease List, with about 80 per cent attributed to genetic factors.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for KL, parts of Selangor, Johor, Sarawak and three states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several areas across the country, including parts of Perlis, Kedah, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Johor and Sarawak. The areas involved are Perlis; Kedah districts of Langkawi, Kubang Pasu and Kota Setar; Selangor districts of Gombak and Hulu Langat; Kuala Lumpur; Negeri Sembilan’s Jelebu; Johor districts of Mersing, Kulai, Kota Tinggi and Johor Bahru; and Kuching, Sarawak. The warning was issued at 4pm today.

items.title: Six brothers charged with trafficking 118g of heroin in Ipoh
items.summary: IPOH, July 28 — Six siblings were charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with trafficking 118.87 grams of heroin last week. Muhammad Affandi Zulkafli, 41, Muhammad Khairul Azmil Zulkafli, 40, Shahrul Azwan Zulkafli, 38, Mohamad Shah Herman Zulkafli, 35, Muhamad Amirul Zulkafli, 29, and Mohamad Hafizi Zulkafli, 27, all unemployed, nodded after the charge was read out before Magistrate Norizan Riduan. According to the charge, the six brothers allegedly trafficked 118.87 grams of heroin at an unnumbered hut beside a house along Laluan Usaha, Kampung Che Zainal Tambahan 1, Chemor, at about 9.20pm on July 21.

items.title: Police: All Rohingya refugees relocated to KL headquarters hold valid UNHCR documents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — All the 110 Rohingya refugees relocated to the Kuala Lumpur Police Contingent Headquarters (IPK) yesterday possess valid documents issued by the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), according to police. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the verification was made following screening and documentation processes conducted on the group of refugees at Dataran Wira within the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters. “During the relocation at about 8.50pm, a total of 110 Rohingya refugees, along with three other foreign nationals, were transferred to the Kuala Lumpur police headquarters with the cooperation of UNHCR.

items.title: Felda settler killed in Jempol crash with lorry after motorcycle enters opposite lane
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — A Felda settler was killed after the motorcycle he was riding entered the opposite lane and collided with a lorry along Kilometer 18 of Jalan Bahau-Kemayan in Jempol, Negeri Sembilan, this morning. Jempol district police chief Superintendent Norhisham Mustapar said the crash at about 11.25am involved a Hino lorry driven by a 53-year-old man travelling from Bahau towards Triang, Pahang, and a Honda C100 motorcycle ridden by the 73-year-old victim, Kosmo! “Upon reaching the scene, as the lorry driver was travelling straight, the victim’s motorcycle from the opposite direction suddenly entered the lorry’s path, causing a collision involving the front right side of the lorry.

items.title: Sarawak crocodile sighting near Sibu flyover sparks public warning
items.summary: SIBU, July 28 — The sight of a crocodile lurking in a pond near the Jalan Oya-Sibu Jaya flyover has prompted a warning for the public on social media. Licensed crocodile hunter Jeferry Siew shared a video of the sighting on a Facebook post, which warned those who frequented the pond for recreational fishing to always exercise caution. In the clip, Siew expressed concern that the crocodile might have been deliberately released into the pond.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan polls: EC targets voter turnout of 75pc on Saturday
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — The Election Commission (EC) is targeting a voter turnout of between 72 and 75 per cent for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election this Saturday, its chairman, Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun, said. As of 10am, early voter turnout stood at 34.26 per cent. He said the number of eligible early voters had been revised from 22,339 to 16,467 after some voters who initially applied for early voting opted to vote by post instead.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan early voter turnout tops 80pc at 2pm as 20 centres close
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — Two more early polling centres for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, involving security force personnel and their spouses, closed at 2pm today. Earlier, 18 early polling centres closed at noon, while the remaining 18 centres will close at 5pm this evening. Early voting involves 22,339 registered voters.

items.title: No land will be acquired for Port Dickson Smart Port, says Aminuddin
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 28 — The AI-powered Smart Port project in Port Dickson will be developed entirely on land owned by Tanco Holdings Berhad and its subsidiary, Midports Holdings Sdn Bhd, without the need to acquire any additional land, Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun said. He dismissed allegations that the project would involve the acquisition of about 566 hectares (1,400 acres) of land, including village areas, forest reserves, customary land, industrial zones, agricultural land, and residential lots, describing the claims as baseless. Furthermore, there is no customary land in Port Dickson.

items.title: Maritime executive says K8 declaration confusion affecting industry, urges Customs Dept to clarify
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy today urged the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) to provide an immediate explanation on the implementation of the K8 declaration procedure, claiming confusion over its application is affecting petroleum industry operations at Tanjung Langsat Port. He said clarification was needed to ensure industry players clearly understood the interpretation and implementation of the K8 procedure, particularly in relation to the handling of petroleum cargo after it has been unloaded into storage tanks. He also sought clarification on Customs' monitoring procedures after cargo is unloaded into storage tanks, the traceability mechanism linking documentation with the physical cargo, and the procedures to ensure exported cargo corresponds with the original declaration.

items.title: Malaysia eyes new framework to deal with economic crisis risks, says PM’s adviser
items.summary: KUALA LIMPUR, July 28 — The government is looking to establish an economic security framework to strengthen the country's resilience against future crises, says the economic adviser to the Prime Minister's Office Nurhisham Hussein. Themed “Reforms for Resilience: Navigating Uncertainties”, the SS2026, held from July 28-29, features discussions on key economic and financial issues, including economic resilience, wages, cost of living challenges, investments, energy security, Islamic finance and private healthcare costs. Meanwhile, Nurhisham said the government is also actively looking at how Malaysia can attract investments and benefit from the global disruptions.

items.title: Deputy minister: Govt studies new data centre projects to prevent strain on power, water supplies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — All applications for new data centre projects undergo strict assessments to ensure electricity and water supplies to households and local industries are not affected, Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said today. “The government is always careful when approving applications related to data centres,” he said during question time in the Dewan Negara. He said the government had also organised matching programmes between multinational corporations and local companies to help small and medium enterprises become suppliers.

items.title: Govt to launch digital trust strategy, enforcement framework by year-end, says Gobind
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 28 — The Digital Ministry is drafting a comprehensive strategy centred on building trust in emerging technologies, with a targeted rollout by the end of this year, said Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo. Gobind explained that the strategy was originally slated for an earlier release but was rescheduled to prioritise the launch of the national AI Malaysia (AIM) platform. “It also comes back now to us building trust.

items.title: Johor police bust two scam rings operating in Forest City, 335 suspects nabbed
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, July 28 — Johor police have busted two online scam syndicates that operate call centres in Forest City in Iskandar Puteri, following the arrest of 335 suspects that included foreigners recently. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspects were nabbed in an integrated operation carried out simultaneously on 27 residential apartment units and five bungalows which were used as the syndicate’s operations centre. Also present was deputy Johor police chief Hoo Chuan Huat and senior officers.
